day_night_curve.notes: Day/night multiplier curve, sampled at index = timeOfDay * 32. 0 = midnight, 8 (0.25) = sunrise, 16 (0.5) = noon, 24 (0.75) = sunset: the same phase as the renderer's sun arc. The previous curve peaked at sunrise and reached zero by mid-afternoon, so the sky stayed bright while tile light (and germination, and photosynthesis) read 0 for the rest of the day.

rain_gain_per_s.notes: Moisture gain per second during rain

evaporation_per_s.notes: Base moisture loss per second at reference temperature (20°C)

temperature_sun_factor.notes: Additional temperature increase from direct sun (0-1 of max sun intensity)

transpiration_factor.notes: Leaf transpiration rate multiplier (moisture loss per leaf per second at reference temp)

photosynthesis_temp_range.notes: Temperature range around optimum where photosynthesis is >50% (±°C)

absorption_per_s.notes: Minerals/moisture absorbed by roots per second, per unit of node draw. Multiplied by the root node's resource_draw_water / resource_draw_minerals.

absorption_radius.notes: Radius in tiles for root absorption

dead_root_deposit.notes: Minerals deposited per dead root node

photosynthesis_rate.notes: Global multiplier on photosynthetic energy output. Structural biomass does NOT come from photosynthesis; only node growth creates biomass.

photosynthesis_energy_per_second.notes: Base energy per photosynthetic organ per second at full light, full hydration and optimum temperature, before the organ's photosynthesis stat modifier

photosynthesis_water_per_energy.notes: Stored water spent per unit of energy fixed by photosynthesis (transpirational cost of carbon gain)

photosynthesis_mineral_per_energy.notes: Stored minerals spent per unit of energy fixed by photosynthesis (enzyme cofactors such as magnesium in chlorophyll)

water_status_full_fraction.notes: Fraction of water capacity at which the plant counts as fully hydrated for photosynthesis. Below this, carbon gain falls away.

mineral_status_full_fraction.notes: Fraction of mineral capacity at which the plant counts as fully supplied for photosynthesis

night_transpiration_multiplier.notes: Fraction of daytime water loss that continues at night. Stomata close in darkness but rarely fully; measured night transpiration is often 10-30% of daytime.

consumption_trigger_tile_mineral_thresho.notes: Tile mineral threshold for consumption trigger

groundwater_base.notes: Initial water held in the deep soil cavity, in the same units as tile moisture. This is the water table roots reach below the surface layer.

groundwater_capacity.notes: Maximum water a soil cell can hold below the surface. Storm recharge fills this store; capillary rise returns it to the root zone.

groundwater_recharge_fraction.notes: Share of rainfall that reaches the deep store directly (macropores and preferential flow), on top of the runoff that exceeds surface infiltration. This is what makes a storm raise the water table in tens of seconds instead of hours, so the pooled water in a dug cavity is observable.

groundwater_infiltration_fraction.notes: Fraction of rain that exceeds the surface infiltration capacity and becomes deep recharge. Based on a soil-water bucket / Green-Ampt partition: wet soil accepts less rain and sends more to runoff and groundwater.

groundwater_percolation_rate.notes: Fraction per second of soil water above field capacity that drains into the groundwater store.

groundwater_capillary_rise_per_s.notes: Moisture units per second drawn upward from groundwater when the root zone is below field capacity.

groundwater_root_uptake_fraction.notes: Maximum share of a cell's accessible groundwater a deep root can draw per absorption step. Keeps a root system from draining an entire cavity in one tick.

groundwater_root_reserve_fraction.notes: Share of a full cavity that roots cannot draw down. The last of the water stays as a reserve for the soil and for future capillary rise.

groundwater_flow_per_s.notes: Fraction of the water-table head difference that flows downhill per second, from a cell to a lower neighbour. Water finds the low ground of the real terrain, so hollows pool and slopes drain instead of every tile rising together.

groundwater_table_depth_m.notes: Depth of an empty water table below the local surface. A full cavity raises the table to the surface, which is what pools visible water in low ground after a storm.

groundwater_table_smoothing_m.notes: Radius averaged to get the regional ground level the water table sits under. The table is a level, not a copy of the ground: without this it dips into every hollow and follows every dug tunnel down, so no hollow ever holds water. Larger values give broader, flatter bodies of water.

max_light.notes: Maximum light level (allows for magical/super-bright conditions)

max_moisture.notes: Maximum moisture level (allows for flooded/super-saturated conditions)

max_minerals.notes: Maximum mineral level (allows for super-fertilized conditions)
